content.value_statement: Bugs waste time when teams guess at fixes before proving the cause. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through evidence-based debugging.
actual_capabilities: Requires root cause investigation before proposed fixes.
Breaks debugging work into investigation, pattern analysis, hypothesis testing, and implementation phases.
Provides checklists for reading errors, reproducing failures, checking recent changes, and tracing data flow.
Includes techniques for stack trace instrumentation, defense-in-depth validation, and condition-based waiting.
Provides a helper script for locating tests that create unwanted files or state.
limitations: It does not diagnose issues automatically without project evidence.
Some examples reference TypeScript, shell, Git, and macOS signing workflows.
The included helper script runs local tests and should only be used in trusted repositories.
It cannot replace human judgment for production incidents or rollback decisions.

use_cases.title: Investigate Recurring Bugs
use_cases.description: Trace a failure from symptom to original trigger before changing code.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Flaky Tests
use_cases.description: Replace timing guesses with condition-based waiting and clear verification.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Coding Sessions
use_cases.description: Keep Claude, Codex, or Claude Code from proposing fixes before evidence is gathered.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Bug Investigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use systematic debugging for this bug. First list the observed failure, reproduction steps, recent changes, and missing evidence before suggesting any fix.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Failing Test
prompt_templates.prompt: A test is failing. Use the skill to trace the failure backward through callers, identify where bad data enters, and state one hypothesis.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Broken and Working Paths
prompt_templates.prompt: Find a working example of the same pattern, compare it with the broken path, and list differences before proposing a minimal test.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Failed Debugging Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Several fixes have failed. Review the evidence, identify untested assumptions, decide whether the architecture should be questioned, and propose next steps.

output_examples.input: A payment test expects completed status but receives pending status.
output_examples.output: The response first lists the observable failure, recent changes, and a reproduction plan. It then states one hypothesis and one minimal test.

output_examples.input: A flaky async test uses a fixed delay before checking results.
output_examples.output: The response recommends waiting for the actual event or state change, adds a clear timeout, and verifies the failure disappears.

output_examples.input: A Git command runs in the wrong directory during tests.
output_examples.output: The response traces the empty directory value back through callers and proposes validation at each layer.

best_practices: Capture the error, reproduction steps, and recent changes before proposing any fix.
Test one hypothesis at a time with the smallest useful change.
Add a failing test or clear reproduction before changing production code.
anti_patterns: Stacking multiple fixes before proving which one changes the outcome.
Using longer sleeps to hide timing bugs without identifying the condition.
Fixing the symptom location when the invalid value entered earlier.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents debug bugs, failed tests, build failures, and unexpected behavior through a structured investigation process.

faq.question: Does it require automated tests?
faq.answer: It prefers a failing test or clear reproduction, but it can also guide manual evidence gathering when tests are unavailable.

faq.question: Can it be used during production incidents?
faq.answer: Yes, but incident response still needs human judgment about mitigation, rollback, and customer impact.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides guidance and an optional helper script; the user or agent decides what to run.

faq.question: Is it only for TypeScript projects?
faq.answer: No. Several examples use TypeScript, but the debugging process applies to most software systems.

faq.question: What happens after repeated failed fixes?
faq.answer: The skill tells the agent to stop, re-analyze assumptions, and consider whether the architecture is wrong.
